  "content": "# Themes and CSS

Purpose: create, edit or activate a custom CSS theme, and know what its CSS does to the interface. A theme is one document-wide `<style>` for the whole app, stored raw and cleaned only at injection.

Actions: reads `theme.list|active|get`; writes `theme.create|update|setActive` (aliases `theme.set`, `theme.activate`; a `themes.` prefix is normalized). There is no `theme.delete` — never claim you removed a theme; that is the Theme Library trash control. `mari themes` mirrors this in the CLI (`--apply` for writes).

## What the CSS can reach

The active theme is one `<style>` in the document head for the entire app — not scoped to chat, not shadow-DOM, not per-panel: what it matches, it repaints. The server keeps the raw string, so a stored theme is not "already safe".

Kept on purpose, because a theme may repaint the app: `position: fixed`, `:has()`, `content:`, `!important`, global `@keyframes`/`@property` names and theme-token overrides. It can overlay, hide, move or imitate any control, an approval card included — so never hide, move, fake or cover a control (approval cards, dialogs, composers, inputs, placeholders), keep text legible, and never present a theme as a way to change behaviour, permissions or approvals. It changes paint and layout, which is exactly why it can hide a control.

Removed at render, silently, so the theme just looks different with no error:

- `url()` outside the `data:` allowlist becomes `url(about:invalid)`; allowed types are `image/`, `font/`, `application/font*`, `application/x-font*`.
- `@import` and `@namespace` are stripped; `@font-face` survives only with at least one `url()`, all of them font `data:` URIs, and no `local()`.
- `expression(`, `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `behavior` and `-moz-binding` are removed; `:visited` becomes `:link`; an `image-set()` holding a `var()` or an external URL is rejected whole.
- Escaped keywords are decoded before the checks, comments are stripped, and a literal `</style>` is inert text, not a breakout.

Embed images and fonts as `data:` URIs, and expect no warning when a vector is dropped.

**A theme for the app sets tokens in `:root`** (and in `[data-theme="light"]` / `[data-theme="dark"]` for each scheme): the core colours (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--card`, `--sidebar`, `--border`…) and the theme tokens and part hooks listed in `docs/appearance/theme-author-guide.md` (`--mari-font-*`, `--mari-top-bar-*`, `--mari-app-backdrop`, `--mari-ambient`, `--mari-weather-*`, `[data-mari-part="…"]`). A name that is in neither that guide nor this handbook, such as `--mari-window-accent`, is read by nothing and changes nothing on screen. For how the theme should look and what to check, read `builtin-theme-design` too.

Public hooks: `.mari-window`, `.mari-drawer`, `.mari-window-bubble`, the `--mari-window-*` and `--mari-drawer-*` variables (`--mari-window-font-family` sets lettering; `--mari-window-ornament` replaces or, as `none`, hides the title ornament) and `data-presentation` (`window`, `sheet`, `menu`). Chat surfaces add `.mari-chat-style-surface|conversation|text|control` and `--mari-chat-*`, which override the window variables; conversation bubbles keep their own shape. The three chat-widget colour options are independent and **off by default**: they participate only when `data-chat-widget-apply-colors="true"`, so setting a variable alone does nothing. Dottore and Prof. Mari are chat-widget presets, not theme rows — a theme can repaint them, not activate as one.

## Write contract

- An **applied** theme write returns `readBack` (`verified`, `mismatch`, `unavailable`), `setActive` included; a dry run or a blocked plan returns none. Never tell the user you must re-read after an applied theme write; on `mismatch` read and report the difference, on `unavailable` read before claiming success.
- `theme.create` writes unless you send `apply: false`; `theme.update` and `theme.setActive` need `apply: true`: sent without `apply` they are refused, and `apply: false` returns `mode: "dry-run"` with nothing written.
- **`apply` is top-level only.** It is read from the command arguments, never from `data`, `patch` or `theme`: a create with `data.apply:false` still writes, and an update with `patch.apply:true` still previews. Both fail silently.
- `theme.create` may activate in the same plan: `activate: true` (or `active: true`) clears every other row and inserts this one active; absent, it is inactive. Create inactive unless the user asked you to switch it on, and send them to **Library → Settings → Appearance → CSS Themes** to try it.
- Only `name` and `css` are written; an update keeps the theme package (pictures, fonts, credits, thumbnail, suggested settings). Add a picture with `mari images generate --target theme-image --theme <id> --name <name>` (the prompt is sent as written, without the user's style profiles or prefixes), then `mari images assign --asset <id> --target theme-image --theme <id> --name <name> --apply`; the CSS uses it as `url("theme:name.webp")`. `mari images adjust --source <asset-id>` crops, trims, clears a flat background, resizes, flips, rotates or tints a preview first. `theme.get` lists pictures by name and size, never their data.
- **Starter themes** (ids starting `starter-`) are read-only gallery downloads: an update is refused, and the id prefix is reserved. The user makes an editable copy with **Clone + Edit** in CSS Themes (it keeps the pictures). Copying a starter's CSS into `theme.create` loses its art.
- `id` is top-level only (`id`/`themeId`) and a caller id is used as-is. `data.id`, `isActive`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are dropped. Create fields in `data`: `name`, `css` (both required non-empty), `installedAt`, `activate`. Update fields in `patch`, `data` or `theme`: only `name` and `css` are read, and top-level copies override the record.
- `theme.list` returns summaries with `cssLength` (characters, not bytes), never the CSS; read one row with `theme.get` or `theme.active`. `list` takes `active: true` and `limit` (default 50, max 1000).
- Caps: name 200 characters (checked on `app_data` too); CSS 256 KiB (262144 UTF-8 bytes), enforced on the REST path only — `app_data` will store CSS the Theme Library can then never save. Stay far under it.
- **`css` replaces the whole stylesheet.** An update that sends one changed rule deletes every other rule: `theme.get`, change the rule in that text, send all of it back.
- When the output limit is small (your workspace rules say so, or a reply was cut at it), a stylesheet cannot go in parts, because every update replaces all of it: keep it to `:root` token overrides and a few hook rules. When the look needs more than one reply holds, say so and offer a smaller version; never send a cut stylesheet.
- Dropped on their own: blank `css` or `name` on update (so **you cannot clear a theme's CSS** — send replacement CSS), `installedAt` and `activate` on update, unknown keys. An update whose only fields were dropped throws `theme.update needs a patch with name or css`. A taken id blocks a create (`Theme id <id> already exists`); a duplicate name and CSS still inserts and only notices `A theme with the same name and CSS already exists`.
- A zero-change apply (identical CSS, re-activating the active row) writes nothing and returns `readBack` `unavailable` with `no applied changes to read back`.

## Workflow

1. `theme.list` for ids, then `theme.get` for the row you will touch — done when you hold its full `css` text. Skip the list when the id is known.
2. Read `docs_read` on `docs/appearance/custom-css-themes.md` before writing CSS you have not seen there, and reuse its class, variable and `data-` names — done when every selector you write appears there or in the reach section above. Re-read the reach section before any rule that positions, hides or covers something.
3. Write the stylesheet as one string, preferring `:root` token overrides and public hooks; one line is fine, escaped newlines are normalized on read.
4. Create with `activate: true` when the look should apply now, otherwise inactive — done when the write returns `readBack` `verified` and you have named the tokens you changed.

## Activation

"Active" is one row with `isActive` true in the server's `custom_themes` table: one install-wide setting synced to every device, never per-chat or per-character. Per-chat styling is Card CSS, a separate mechanism with a stricter sanitizer; never offer a theme as a per-chat change. `theme.setActive` plans over every row, so the target turns active and all others inactive in one reversible change card. When your switch to a theme is applied, the user's tab puts the previous theme back on the server and asks **Keep this theme?** for 15 seconds, the same as picking it in CSS Themes: Keep makes it active everywhere, no answer goes back. So right after a switch, `theme.active` can still name the previous theme; tell the user to press Keep rather than re-sending the switch. Switching to Default never asks. Deactivate with no id, or with `default`, `none`, `null` or `off` (case-insensitive) — Default Theme, not an error. An unknown id is `Theme not found`. `setActive` never edits CSS or the name.

A theme created with one of those reserved ids (`none`, `default`, `off`, `null`) stores fine but can never be activated: `setActive` reads the id as "deactivate". Pick a real id.

Do not describe activation as admin-gated: on the REST route it is deliberately open while create, update and delete are privileged, and the `theme.*` path does not consult that gate — report what the action returned instead of asserting a permission rule.

The Theme Library activates on save and leaves activation alone when editing. A backup or profile import brings every theme in inactive — `N active custom theme(s) will be imported inactive so profile CSS cannot take effect before review.` — so activate explicitly after a restore.

## Per-chat Card CSS

A card styles its own chat with `<style>` blocks inside its **Creator Notes**, extracted at render as one `#marinara-card-css` element. There is no CSS action: write the note with `character.update` (or `persona.update`), splicing the block into the existing text, `apply:true`.

- **You cannot turn it on.** The switch is **Chat Settings → Card Theming** (`cardCssMode`: `disabled`, `exclusive` or `chat`) and only that panel writes it. In Roleplay chats the section is always there (it also holds the inline name-color switch), but the mode buttons appear only when a card carries a `<style>` block. Send the user there, say which mode you wrote for, and ask them to reload before judging.
- The browser sanitizes at render, silently: `position: fixed` becomes `absolute`, `:has()`/`!important` and theme-token declarations are dropped, and `display`, `visibility`, `opacity`, `transform` and `content:` survive. Write paint only — never a rule that covers, hides or imitates a control. There is no byte cap; keep it small, it is parsed on every render.
- Reuse the class, variable and `data-card-css` names from `docs/appearance/card-css-theming.md`; do not invent selectors from the theme variables.

## Errors and fixes

Wording is exact; a `readBack` status is not an error.

| Message                                                                                                                                                    | Fix                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `theme css is required (none was sent): send a non-empty "css" top-level, or inside "data".`                                                               | A theme cannot be created empty; send at least one rule.         |
| `theme id is required (none was sent): send a non-empty "id" or "themeId" top-level. If you do not know it, use the matching list or search action first.` | Resolve the row before reading or updating it.                   |
| `theme.update needs a patch with name or css`                                                                                                              | Every field sent was dropped or unknown; send a real change.     |
| `Theme not found`                                                                                                                                          | The `setActive` target does not exist; re-list before switching. |
| `Theme name must be 200 characters or fewer`                                                                                                               | Shorten the name.                                                |
| `Theme id <id> already exists`                                                                                                                             | Choose another id, or update that row.                           |
| `A theme with the same name and CSS already exists`                                                                                                        | A notice only; the row was still created.                        |

## Worked example

One `app_data` call per line, ids pinned: create and activate in one call, check it, then the requested accent change — the whole stylesheet with one value changed — and a return to Default.

```
{"action":"theme.create","id":"mari-aurora","data":{"name":"Aurora Nocturne","css":":root { --background: #0a0a12; --primary: #b388ff; }","activate":true},"reason":"Adds the Aurora palette the user asked for.","apply":true}
{"action":"theme.list","limit":5}
{"action":"theme.get","id":"mari-aurora"}
{"action":"theme.update","id":"mari-aurora","patch":{"css":":root { --background: #0a0a12; --primary: #c4a0ff; }"},"reason":"Brightens the accent the user picked.","apply":true}
{"action":"theme.setActive","id":"none","reason":"Returns to the Default theme.","apply":true}
```

Read the results in order: the create returns `verified` with `mari-aurora` active and no other row active; `theme.list` shows `cssLength` and no `css`; the update returns `verified` and keeps `--background`, because it resent the whole stylesheet; the last line leaves no active row. The same update without `apply` would return `mode: "dry-run"`, write nothing and show the user nothing — never send one as a preview.

## Where the detail lives

For tokens, parts, pictures, backdrops, day/night and the safety rules, read `docs_read docs/appearance/theme-author-guide.md` (start at `Colour tokens`, `Hooks`, `Pictures`, `Day and night`, `Safety`); for weather, `docs/appearance/theme-weather.md`. For a card's own styling read `docs_read docs/appearance/card-css-theming.md` at `What Card CSS is`, `The Card Theming modes`, `Writing Card CSS` and `Security and limits`, then `docs_read` in `docs/appearance/custom-css-themes.md`: `What a custom theme is`, `Creating a theme`, `Activating a theme`, `The CSS variable reference`, then `Styling chat windows and drawers` with its `Classes`, `Data attributes` and `Variables` headings, then `Size and name limits` and `Themes and Card CSS`. In `docs/appearance/appearance-settings.md`: `Chat Buttons & Windows`, `Theme` (Custom Mouse Pointer and `Reset Appearance`, which turns off any active custom theme). `Who can change themes` in custom-css-themes.md: installing needs the admin secret from another device, picking an installed theme does not."
}

  "content": "# Theme design and review

Purpose: help the user make a theme that looks finished on every screen, or review one they already have. This handbook is about **how the theme should look and what to check**. For the `theme.*` actions, `apply`, `readBack` and errors, read the built-in **Themes and CSS** handbook first; both apply.

The reference for every token, part and slot is `docs/appearance/theme-author-guide.md` (read it with `docs_read`; start at `Colour tokens`, `Hooks`, `Pictures`, `Backdrops`, `Ambient overlay`, `Day and night`, `Safety`). Weather is in `docs/appearance/theme-weather.md`. Never invent a token or `data-mari-part` name: if it isn't in those docs, it does nothing.

## What a theme can do here

- **Tokens** on `:root` (all schemes), `[data-theme="light"]` and `[data-theme="dark"]`: the core colours (`--background`, `--card`, `--primary`, `--sidebar`, `--border`…), the new-layout tokens (`--ov-*`, `--mari-selected-tint`) and the theme tokens (`--mari-font-*`, `--mari-top-bar-*`, `--mari-home-widget-*`, `--mari-chat-*`, `--mari-page-veil`, `--mari-accent-text`, `--mari-confirm-scrim`, long-reply tokens such as `--mari-message-measure`…).
- **Parts**: `[data-mari-part="…"]` hooks for messages (`message` is the whole full-width row; paint `bubble`, or each bubble sits in a second box), avatars, the composer, the top bar, page titles, the page surface every Library page/editor/Settings/Docs sits on (`page`), Home widgets, time, dialogue, VN boxes. Prefer these over internal classes.
- **Art**: `--mari-app-backdrop` (and `-layers`), `--mari-ambient` (under the bars, mostly see-through), `--mari-home-art`, `border-image` frames, `--mari-focus-frame`. Pictures are named `url("theme:name.webp")` and live in the theme's package, not in the CSS.
- **Weather**: `--mari-weather-*` tokens restyle rain, snow, fog, petals, lightning; `data-mari-weather` / `data-mari-sky` on `<html>` let art follow the story weather. A theme can thin weather out but never switch it off.
- **Day and night**: style both `[data-theme]` sides. Users may follow system or time of day.
- **Per-chat looks**: `:root[data-chat-tags~="horror"]`, `[data-chat-open-mode]`.
- **Message templates (HTML)** exist but are off unless the user turns on "Allow themes with HTML". Don't plan a theme around one unless the user asks.

Internal classes (`.ov-*`, Tailwind) work but can change in any update. When you must use one, say so in a CSS comment and keep it to shape and colour.

## What you can't do from chat (tell the user plainly)

- **Fonts, thumbnails, credits, suggested settings** live in the theme package. `theme.create` and `theme.update` only write `name` and `css`, and an update keeps the package as it is. The user adds those in **Library → Settings → Appearance → CSS Themes → their theme → Pictures and sharing details**. Pictures you can add yourself (next section).
- **Starter themes** (ids starting `starter-`) are read-only downloads from the gallery. Never `theme.update` one: the next gallery update would overwrite it. To change one, have the user click **Clone + Edit** (the copy icon) on it, which keeps its pictures, then work on the copy. Copying its CSS into `theme.create` loses all its art.
- **Trying a theme**: picking a theme in CSS Themes asks **Keep this theme?** for 15 seconds. When you switch one on (`theme.setActive`, or `activate: true`), the user's tab asks the same question and goes back if nobody answers. Still prefer creating the theme **inactive** and letting the user pick it when they're ready to look. Activate it yourself only when they ask you to, and tell them to press **Keep theme**.
- **Seeing the screen**: you can't. Every visual check below ends with you asking the user to look at a named spot, or to send a screenshot.
- `theme.get` shows a theme's pictures by name, size and the `url("theme:…")` to use, not the picture itself; use `mari images look` to see one. You still can't see the app with the theme on it.

## Pictures for a theme

When the user has an image connection (`mari images connections`), you can make a theme's art: backdrops, the Home picture, tiles, frames, icons.

1. The theme must exist and be the user's own (create it inactive first; for a starter, have them **Clone + Edit** and use the copy's id).
2. `mari images generate --prompt "<your prompt>" --target theme-image --theme <id> --name <name> [--width <n> --height <n>]`. With `--target theme-image` your prompt goes to the provider **exactly as you wrote it**: the user's image style profiles, prompt prefixes, LoRAs and style reference are left out, because those are set up for character art. So write the whole prompt yourself: subject, style, palette, "no people, no text" when that is what you want. Size it for the job: wide (e.g. 1536×864) for a backdrop, square for a tile or icon, and a 9-slice frame with a plain middle. Add `--count 3` (up to 4) to make several versions in one go so the user can pick; each is its own request, so it takes that many times as long.
3. You see what you made: generate, edit and adjust attach the pictures to their result (every version with `--count`). Look at them before you describe or pick one: subject, palette against the theme, a calm area where text will sit, leftover backgrounds, text or watermarks the model drew. `mari images look --source <asset>[,<asset>…]` (up to 4) or `mari images look --target theme-image --theme <id> --name <name>` shows you any picture again. Then show the user the preview and wait for a yes. Make another if they don't like it; nothing is saved to the theme yet.
   - To fix a preview without generating again, use `mari images adjust --source <asset-id>` with `--crop left,top,width,height` (pixels or %), `--trim` (cut empty edges), `--transparent` (the corner colour becomes see-through where it touches the edge; `--transparent #hex`, `--tolerance 0-255`, `--everywhere` to clear it inside too), `--resize 512` or `--resize 1920x1080 --fit cover`, `--flip horizontal`, `--rotate 90`, `--tint #hex`. It makes a new preview (PNG, transparency kept) and leaves the original; show that one too. Image generators rarely give real transparency, so for an icon, sticker or frame ask for "on a plain flat white background" and clear it with `--transparent`.
4. `mari images assign --asset <asset-id> --target theme-image --theme <id> --name <name> --apply`. It is saved as WebP (at most 2560 px a side; small pictures stay lossless, so pixel art and frames stay crisp). The same name replaces the old picture. The result gives the `css` to paste, e.g. `url("theme:night-sky.webp")`, and how much of the 6 MiB package is used.
5. Put that `url()` in the CSS with `theme.update` (send the whole stylesheet). Remove a picture with `mari images delete --target theme-image --theme <id> --name <name> --apply`.

A picture is art, not text: keep words, labels and the app's controls out of it, and check readability on top of it (Step 5).

## Hard rules (a theme that breaks these gets switched off, or rejected)

- The top bar, its tabs and icons, the sidebar and its chat rows, Ctrl+K and the message box keep their place and stay visible and clickable. Restyle them (colour, font, border, radius, shadow, a background picture), never hide, move, shrink, fade, filter or cover them.
- **On phones and tablets a theme never adds rows.** Mobile users want every pixel of chat. Decoration goes inside the normal top bar height, not in a new strip under it. If art behind the top bar makes buttons hard to see, give the buttons opaque backing (`--mari-top-bar-plate`, `--mari-top-bar-plate-radius`), don't move the art into its own row.
- Opaque or near-opaque backing behind every button and label that sits on busy art. Readability beats the picture.
- No scripts, no outside addresses (`@import`, remote `url()`, web fonts by link). Pictures and fonts go in the package.
- No text that asks for keys, passwords or sign-ins, claims to be the app ("security alert", "verified"), holds a phone number or web address, or runs past 80 letters in one `content:`. No fake dialogs, fake buttons or relabelled buttons.
- Respect the user's choices: Accessibility settings, Reduce motion, Theme art strength, High contrast and the weather toggle always win. Use tokens instead of literal colours on your own selectors so High contrast can reach them.
- Every hover effect goes inside `@media (hover: hover)`. Touch screens get no hover looks, including sticky ones after a tap.
- Keep the app's headings and labels. Don't hide a section title (e.g. Chat Settings) to tidy a look, even if the theme adds its own title bar.
- Plain names for anything the theme labels. No cute renames of app areas.

## Step 1: agree on the idea

Ask (one short message, offer defaults): the mood or reference, Light/Dark/both, which devices they use, whether they want art (they supply it) and weather styling, and whether this is a new theme or a change to one.

Then pick **one structural idea** and say it in a sentence before writing CSS, e.g. "every container is a coffin shape with cut corners", "everything is a soft glass capsule", "hard square panels with offset shadows, like a field manual". A theme is a shape language plus a palette, not just a palette. If the user wants several themes, each one needs its own structural idea; two themes that only differ in colour read as reskins.

Done when the user has agreed to the idea, or told you to go ahead.

## Step 2: write a shape spec first

Before any rule, write down (in a CSS comment at the top of the theme):

- **Shape family**: one of square (0), small round (4-8px), round (10-16px), capsule (999px), or a chamfer/cut corner. Which elements get which: containers, fields (inputs, selects, search boxes, text areas), buttons, pills/tags, avatars.
- **Border**: width and style for containers, fields and buttons.
- **Shadow style**: one kind (soft blur, hard offset, glow, or none) used by every sibling.
- **Selected and focus look**: an inset ring or fill, never an outset ring that makes the selected item bigger than its neighbours.

Most of the back-and-forth on past themes was this: shapes that didn't match. The spec is how you avoid it.

## Step 3: build, in this order

1. Colours for both schemes (`:root`, then `[data-theme="light"]` and `[data-theme="dark"]`).
2. Fonts (`--mari-font-ui`, `--mari-font-heading`, `--mari-font-chat`), and long-reply tokens for roleplay (`--mari-message-measure`, `--mari-chat-line-height`, `--mari-dialogue-weight`).
3. Shapes from the spec, applied to **every** surface that holds the same kind of thing (see the coverage list in Step 4). Style the shared hook (`[data-mari-part="page"]`, `.mari-window`, `.mari-drawer`) rather than one page's class, so Lorebooks gets the same panel as Characters.
4. Art and the top bar (plates behind controls on art), then weather.
5. Hover inside `@media (hover: hover)`; touch-only tweaks inside `@media (pointer: coarse)`.

Keep the stylesheet well under 256 KiB, and send the whole stylesheet on every update (Themes and CSS explains why).

## Step 4: the shape and border checklist

Go through these against the CSS you wrote, then ask the user to look at the named spots. These are the mistakes that kept coming back.

**Same shape for things in a row**

- [ ] Buttons, selects, search boxes and toggles that sit in one toolbar share one radius and one height. A pill search box next to square buttons is wrong; so is a round view toggle beside square filters.
- [ ] Sibling cards, sibling chips and sibling buttons share radius, padding, border and shadow.
- [ ] Composer buttons (attach, emoji, send, the ^ button) are the same size, so their pressed circles and shadows match.

**A border, glow, shadow or ring takes the shape of what it wraps**

- [ ] A pill-shaped border around a rounded-rectangle button (or the reverse) is wrong. Outline, glow, `box-shadow` and focus ring all follow the element's own `border-radius`.
- [ ] Nested corners are concentric: outer radius = inner radius + the gap between them. A rounded row inside a rounded drawer with too small an outer radius looks pinched.
- [ ] **Never a square shape inside a rounded container**, and never a rounded one inside a square or chamfered container. Common spots: Chat settings rows inside the drawer, a header strip or divider running square into a popover's rounded top corners, the list/grid toggle inside a rounded toolbar, the tag-filter popover's search box, Settings plates.
- [ ] No square backdrop or shadow behind a rounded shape (corners poke out), and no page colour showing through at a panel's rounded corners.
- [ ] A selected item's ring doesn't make it bigger than its neighbours (use an inset `box-shadow` or a fill).
- [ ] Underlines on active tabs don't bend around the tab's rounded bottom corners into a crescent.

**Shadows**

- [ ] One shadow style for the whole theme. Don't mix a soft blurred popover with hard offset shadows elsewhere.
- [ ] Shadows of things that touch don't merge into a smudge (e.g. a swipe counter sitting on message chips).
- [ ] Focus is visible: the focus shadow differs from the resting shadow.
- [ ] No text-shadow glow on small text in Light mode (it looks doubled).

**Coverage: give the shape to every surface, not just the obvious one**

- [ ] Chat settings drawer (rows, fields, Edit button, star), on desktop and as the phone sheet.
- [ ] Library toolbars on every page (Characters, Personas, Lorebooks, Presets, Regex, Connections, Agents), Chats list toolbar, tag-filter popover, sort menus.
- [ ] Ctrl+K, confirm dialogs, toasts, dropdown menus, the long-press sheet on phones, the character profile bubble.
- [ ] Settings (Appearance and one other tab), Docs, an editor (character, lorebook entry, preset).
- [ ] Home widgets including Professor Mari's, Recent chats, What's new.
- [ ] Split view's narrow side and its slim bar.

## Step 5: readability and layout checklist

- [ ] Body text at least 4.5:1 against what is actually behind it (picture included); top-bar labels at least 3:1 everywhere, including small status words like "Online" on a tab.
- [ ] Both Light and Dark checked. A colour that passes at night can fail by day.
- [ ] Every Library page has the same panel behind it (style `[data-mari-part="page"]`).
- [ ] Text over art has a plate, veil (`--mari-page-veil`) or wash. Version labels, timestamps and swipe counters too.
- [ ] Nothing cut mid-letter at narrow widths (phone, narrow split view, big theme fonts). Prefer smaller text or an ellipsis to a new row.
- [ ] Icons centred in their buttons and inside their fields, never overlapping text.
- [ ] Spacing even inside cards; dividers as wide as the box they belong to; tip and help boxes aligned with the content column.
- [ ] Long roleplay replies stay comfortable (line length about 60-75 characters, no bold slabs of dialogue).
- [ ] Phones: top bar is the normal height; Conversation / Roleplay / Game stay on one row on Home.

## Step 6: hand it over and check with the user

1. Create the theme inactive (unless the user asked you to switch it on), and tell them where to try it: **Library → Settings → Appearance → CSS Themes**, pick it, then **Keep theme** within 15 seconds.
2. Give a short, specific look-list from Steps 4 and 5 for the screens they use, both Light and Dark, and ask for a screenshot of anything that looks off. Name exact spots ("the search box and the buttons beside it on the Lorebooks page"), not "check the theme".
3. If the app switched the theme off or refused it, ask what message it showed. It names the reason (covered top bar, unreadable labels, unsafe text, an outside address). Fix that reason; don't work around the guard.
4. Remind them of the way back: Esc three times, `?safe` at the end of the address, or Ctrl+K → "Custom theme".

## Reviewing an existing theme

When the user asks "what's wrong with my theme" or for polish:

1. Get the CSS (`theme.get`, or ask them to paste it for a big theme).
2. List every `border-radius`, `box-shadow`, `outline` and `border` value and which selectors use it. Flag mixed radii among siblings, shapes that disagree with their container, and more than one shadow style.
3. Check the hard rules and Step 5 against the CSS.
4. Report findings grouped by screen, most visible first, each with the selector and the fix. Change nothing until the user says which to fix; then send the whole stylesheet with only those changes.

## Worked example: the shape spec

```css
/* Shape spec — Harbor Glass
   idea: frosted capsules on a sea backdrop
   containers 16px · fields and buttons 999px (capsule) · tags 999px · avatars round
   border 1px rgba(255,255,255,.35) · shadow soft only: 0 4px 14px -6px rgba(0,40,80,.45)
   selected: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--primary) · focus: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 45%, transparent) */
:root {
  --mari-tokens-version: 1;
  --radius: 16px;
  --mari-top-bar-plate: color-mix(in srgb, var(--card) 92%, transparent);
  --mari-top-bar-plate-radius: 999px;
}
[data-mari-part="page"] {
  border-radius: 16px;
}
.mari-drawer {
  border-radius: 16px;
}
@media (hover: hover) {
  [data-mari-part="bubble"]:hover {
    box-shadow: 0 4px 14px -6px rgba(0, 40, 80, 0.45);
  }
}
```

Every row inside the 16px drawer then uses a radius of 16px minus the drawer's padding (or capsules all the way through), never a square row."
